quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 44

questions.question: What can lower the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed when roads are wet.
Keep tires filled to the correct air pressure.
Replace tires with worn tread.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your vehicle slides on a thin layer of water between the tires and road. Low tire pressure and worn tread increase hydroplaning risk. Speeding also increases this risk.

questions.question: If you stop at a railroad crossing with more than one track, what should you do?

options.text: Wait to proceed until you can see clearly down all tracks.
Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
Go through as soon as the train passes.
Go through when one track is free.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait to proceed until you can see clearly down all tracks.
questions.explanation: Do not move as soon as a train passes. Always wait until you can see clearly down all tracks before crossing. Another train may be approaching on a different track.

questions.question: Railroad crossings should always be considered:

options.text: Safe to cross, since a train is unlikely to come.
Dangerous.
Safe places to park your car.
Places where you must always stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dangerous.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Look and listen for trains from both directions on all tracks. Follow all signs, signals, and flaggers. Never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: When driving through curves, the most important thing is to:

options.text: Drive at the speed limit as you enter, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before entering the curve.
Speed up gently before entering the curve.
Drive at the speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering the curve.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle's momentum can make it hard to turn. To stay in control, slow down before you enter the curve.

questions.question: Can you drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public highway?

options.text: Yes, as long as you are not driving.
Yes, if you are in the back seat.
Yes, if you are in the back of a pickup truck.
No, under no circumstances.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, under no circumstances.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink or carry open alcohol in a vehicle on any public road. You cannot keep an open alcohol container in any seating area of a motor vehicle on a public road.

questions.question: When backing up, you should:

options.text: Use only your mirrors.
Flash your lights.
Open your door to check if it is safe.
Turn your head and look through the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your vehicle before backing up. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat. Look through the rear window by turning your head. Do not rely only on mirrors or sensors.

questions.question: What does this road sign indicate?

options.text: The maximum safe speed for a residential area.
The maximum safe speed for an expressway exit.
The maximum safe speed for an expressway entrance.
The maximum safe speed for a work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe speed for an expressway exit.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the maximum safe speed for a highway exit. In this example, the safe speed is 30 mph.

questions.question: What affects your ability to stop?

options.text: Signal lights.
Other cars on the road.
The time of day.
The condition of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The condition of the road.
questions.explanation: Road condition greatly affects how quickly you can stop. Reduce your speed when roads are poor to keep control of your vehicle. Driving too fast on slippery roads puts you at risk if you need to stop suddenly.

questions.question: When should you look over your shoulder to check your blind spot?

options.text: When pulling toward or away from a curb.
When turning left or right.
When changing lanes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Check your blind spot every time you change your vehicle's position. This includes turning, changing lanes, and pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Speed up to increase the distance between you.
Slam on your brakes to make them back off.
Change lanes or slowly reduce speed to let them pass.
Ignore them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slowly reduce speed to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Check traffic behind you several times per minute to spot tailgaters or fast-approaching cars. If someone is following too closely, slow down gradually and let them pass. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: You are driving on a two-lane road with no bike lanes. A cyclist is ahead of you going the same direction. How should you safely pass?

options.text: Slow down and wait for no oncoming traffic. Then pass with plenty of space between you and the cyclist.
Keep driving straight. The cyclist should move out of your way.
Do not pass until you reach a traffic light or stop sign.
Honk to let the cyclist know you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and wait for no oncoming traffic. Then pass with plenty of space between you and the cyclist.
questions.explanation: Pass a cyclist like you would pass any other vehicle. Keep at least 3 feet of space from your mirror to the cyclist. Use 5 feet on faster roads or when passing multiple cyclists. Do not honk unless needed—it may startle the rider and cause a crash.

questions.question: What does this sign show?

options.text: Right turn.
Intersection.
Lane change.
Road curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a T intersection is coming up ahead.

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalk, which side should a pedestrian walk on?

options.text: The side with the lightest traffic.
The same side traffic is moving on.
The side facing oncoming traffic.
The side with the heaviest traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: The side facing oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Walk on the side of the road where you can see traffic coming toward you.

questions.question: Why should you signal before turning, changing lanes, or leaving a curb?

options.text: Only if other cars are nearby.
It is good practice and the law requires it.
Only while you are making the move, not before.
Not needed if you move slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is good practice and the law requires it.
questions.explanation: Signal at least 100 feet before turning or changing lanes. Always signal before leaving a curb to tell other drivers what you are doing.

questions.question: What does a solid white line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Lanes go in opposite directions. You cannot pass.
Lanes go in opposite directions. You can pass when safe.
Lanes go in the same direction. You cannot pass.
Lanes go in the same direction. You can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lanes go in the same direction. You cannot pass.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: One-way traffic.
Divided highway ends.
Two-way traffic.
Keep left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway ends.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black lettering on yellow. This sign tells you the divided highway is ending ahead.

questions.question: What is a speed limit?

options.text: The fastest or slowest legal speed on a road in bad conditions.
The fastest or slowest legal speed on a road in good conditions.
The suggested speed for a road in good conditions.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fastest or slowest legal speed on a road in good conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the fastest or slowest legal speed in good conditions. You can drive slower than posted, but never faster. Drive slower in school zones, work zones, or when weather or road conditions are bad.

questions.question: What does a steady yellow light mean?

options.text: Go.
Yield to other cars.
Slow down and get ready to stop.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and get ready to stop.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means red is coming. Slow down and prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely, go through carefully.

questions.question: You are backing out of your driveway and see children playing nearby. What should you do first?

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children.
Honk your horn so they hear you.
Walk behind your car to check if the way is clear.
Tell the children to stay away from the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk behind your car to check if the way is clear.
questions.explanation: Always get out and look behind your vehicle before backing up. Do not rely only on mirrors, especially when children are nearby.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You are about to enter a one-way street from the wrong direction.
U-turns are not allowed.
You can go if the path is clear.
Come to a complete stop before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are about to enter a one-way street from the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: This sign means you are going the wrong way on a one-way street. You risk a head-on collision. Turn around carefully.

questions.question: When driving in fog, which lights should you use?

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
Hazard flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlights in fog. If your vehicle has fog lights, use those too. High beams point upward and bounce off fog, making it harder to see.

questions.question: When do roads become very slippery?

options.text: When it has been raining for an hour or more.
The day after it rains.
For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
Right after the rain has stopped.

questions.correctAnswerText: For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
questions.explanation: Roads are very slippery in the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain. Rain brings oil from the asphalt to the road surface. In hot weather, this gets worse.

questions.question: What does this green arrow on a lane control signal mean?

options.text: You may use this lane.
No traffic is allowed in this lane.
You have the right of way.
You must merge into this lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may use this lane.
questions.explanation: A steady green arrow pointing down means you can use that lane.

questions.question: Can you cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass another vehicle?

options.text: Yes.
No.
Yes, if there is no oncoming traffic.
Yes, if the vehicle ahead is driving under the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: No.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass. You can only cross double yellow lines when turning into a driveway or business entrance.

questions.question: What do orange signs mean?

options.text: Work zone signs.
Regulatory signs.
School zone signs.
Guide signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work zone signs.
questions.explanation: Orange signs warn you about work zones. They are diamond-shaped with black letters and alert you that workers are on or near the highway.

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: A driver must proceed slowly through the intersection.
A driver must stop and then proceed when the way is clear.
A driver must stop and wait for a green light or green arrow.
A driver may turn in the direction the red arrow points.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver must stop and wait for a green light or green arrow.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you must stop completely and stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears. Do not proceed unless a sign says otherwise.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Buggy warning.
Turn right or go straight.
Minimum speed.
Winding road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Buggy warning.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign alerts drivers that buggies may be ahead on the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
Two-way left turn.
Minimum speed limit.
No parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This regulation sign means U-turns are not allowed where it is posted.

questions.question: What is an inattentive driver?

options.text: A driver who stares at objects off the road or daydreams.
A driver who makes eye contact with a passenger while driving.
A driver who only watches the vehicle ahead.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not get distracted by passengers, searching your vehicle, reading, sightseeing, or daydreaming. Keep scanning the road, checking mirrors, and watching your instrument panel. These safe habits keep you focused on driving.

questions.question: What does this sign warn you about?

options.text: An intersection.
A crosswalk.
A railroad crossing.
A blasting zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: A railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: What does this black and yellow sign mean?

options.text: The road to the right is one-way only.
There is a detour to the right due to roadwork ahead.
Slow down. The road ahead turns sharply at a steep angle.
There is a crossroad to your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down. The road ahead turns sharply at a steep angle.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead turns sharply at a steep angle. Slow down before you reach this sharp turn, just as you would at an intersection.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: These parking spaces are for people with disabled parking permits.
A circular intersection is ahead.
Traffic in this lane must turn in the direction shown by the arrow.
These lanes are reserved for buses and carpool vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: These parking spaces are for people with disabled parking permits.
questions.explanation: This sign marks parking spaces reserved only for people with disabled parking permits.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: No passing zone.
Winding road ahead.
Pedestrian crossing.
Low ground railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low ground railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a low ground railroad crossing. The railroad tracks cross the road at a steep slope. Low vehicles may drag or get stuck on the tracks.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: One-way traffic only.
Two-way left turn.
Two-way traffic.
Minimum speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: One-way traffic only.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the direction traffic must go on this street. You must drive in the direction shown by the arrow when entering a one-way street.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Give the motorcycle a full lane to use.
Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.
Allow the motorcycle to use only half a lane.
Share the same lane when passing the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the motorcycle a full lane to use.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle is a full vehicle with the same road rights as any other vehicle. Give it a full lane width. Even if space looks tight, the motorcycle needs room to move safely.

questions.question: When you see this sign, what is your biggest concern?

options.text: Your headlights will be out of alignment because one side of your car is higher.
You might damage a tire by drifting onto the shoulder.
You might hydroplane if the shoulder has water on it.
You might lose control if one wheel drops onto the low shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: You might lose control if one wheel drops onto the low shoulder.
questions.explanation: This sign means the shoulder is lower than the road. If you drift off the road, do not brake hard or turn sharply. This can cause you to lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: When you see railroad tracks, you should:

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
Speed up to cross before the gate goes down.
Drive around a lowered gate.
Not worry about how many tracks there are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Always look and listen for trains at railroad crossings. Slow down and be ready to stop for trains or other vehicles on the tracks.

questions.question: A bicyclist who breaks traffic laws:

options.text: Is allowed to because bicyclists don't have to follow traffic laws.
Can receive a ticket.
Will always get a warning from police.
Will have their bicycle taken.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can receive a ticket.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as car drivers. They must follow traffic laws or they can be ticketed.

questions.question: To enter a freeway, you should:

options.text: Signal, let other traffic pass first, and enter at the same speed as traffic.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must let you in.
Drive slowly to check the traffic.
Always stop completely first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, let other traffic pass first, and enter at the same speed as traffic.
questions.explanation: Signal and enter at the same speed as traffic. Always let other vehicles go first when merging onto a roadway.

questions.question: If a train is close or moving fast enough to be dangerous, you must:

options.text: Slow down and proceed with care.
Wait until the train has completely passed before crossing.
Cross the tracks at your own risk.
Find another route across the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the train has completely passed before crossing.
questions.explanation: Look and listen for trains before crossing railroad tracks. If a train is close or moving fast, do not cross. Wait until it has completely passed. This applies even if there are no signals or the signals are broken.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, which way should you turn the steering wheel?

options.text: Keep the front wheels straight.
In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
In the opposite direction of the skid.
In any direction. It doesn't matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
questions.explanation: Turn the steering wheel in the direction you want the vehicle to go. Once the vehicle begins to straighten, turn the steering wheel back the other way.

questions.question: What do highways use to direct drivers into the correct lanes for turning?

options.text: Flashing red lights
Flashing yellow lights
White lines on the side of the road
White arrows in the middle of the lanes

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows in the middle of the lanes
questions.explanation: Arrows show which lanes to use for specific purposes, such as going straight or turning.

questions.question: How can you help reduce road rage and aggressive driving?

options.text: Allow extra travel time.
Obey posted speed limits.
Use proper turn signals.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To prevent road rage, use proper turn signals, obey speed limits, and allow plenty of travel time.

questions.question: Which traffic light means you should slow down and proceed with caution?

options.text: A flashing yellow light
A flashing red light
A solid yellow light
A solid red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing yellow light
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, proceed carefully, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What is the correct order of colors on a traffic light from top to bottom?

options.text: Red, yellow, green.
Red, green, yellow.
Green, red, yellow.
Green, yellow, red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Red, yellow, green.
questions.explanation: On a vertical traffic signal, red is always on top and green is always on the bottom. On a horizontal signal, red is always on the left and green is always on the right.

questions.question: You are driving on a divided multilane highway and see an emergency vehicle approaching. What should you do?

options.text: Ignore the signal if other lanes are available for the emergency vehicle.
Stop as quickly as you can.
Slow down, move your vehicle to clear the path, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move your vehicle to clear the path, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights, slow down, create a clear path, and stop. Do not try to outrun the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Sharp right turn.
A road joins from the right.
The road turns sharply right, then sharply left.
Winding road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road turns sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead turns sharply to the right and then sharply to the left.

questions.question: What should you do when preparing to turn left?

options.text: Slow down gradually and check your rearview mirror.
Move into the left lane.
Watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before turning left, signal 3 to 5 seconds ahead. Check your rearview mirror and slow down gradually. On a multilane road, move into the left lane before the intersection. Yield to traffic and pedestrians, then turn when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No left turn.
Flagger ahead.
Two-way left turn.
Turn right or go straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: No left turn.
questions.explanation: This is a regulation sign that tells drivers what they must or must not do. This sign means left turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Lanes moving in the same direction are divided by ____ lines.

options.text: Yellow
White
Red
Black

questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes going the same direction. Broken white lines can be crossed to pass. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.
